guitar.evidence: Jimi Hendrix's white Fender Stratocaster (played upside-down/restrung for a right-handed guitar as a left-handed player) is one of the most iconic guitar associations in rock history.

tone.target: wild fuzzed Hendrix lead with wah and feedback
tone.profile: wild fuzzed Hendrix lead with wah and feedback
tone.summary: A raw, high-gain signal chain featuring Fuzz distortion, Wah sweeps, a powerful UK 45 amp model, and vintage cabinet simulation to capture the aggressive, fuzzy sound of Hendrix's live performance.
corrections: swap Fender clean for Marshall crunch

rig.name: Jimi Hendrix - Foxy Lady (Live at Monterey) - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum inherent in high-gain fuzz circuits.
Used as a mild tone shaper/boost for the wah circuit, but kept inactive to prioritize fuzz.
blocks.gap: The primary boost is handled by the Fuzz unit itself. This slot maintains chain integrity.

blocks.purpose: Provides the essential Fuzz Face style saturation and raw bite required for Hendrix's tone.
Essential for the signature wah sweeps and vocal filtering characteristic of the song.
Simulates the powerful, aggressive British Marshall-style crunch needed for live rock performance.
Provides the classic British rock cabinet sound and necessary upper-mid rasp.
Fine-tuning the upper-mids and overall tone to achieve maximum bite and rasp.
blocks.gap: Using a dedicated EQ block for surgical tone shaping is necessary given the 'upper-mid rasp' requirement.

blocks.purpose: Adds a subtle sense of live room ambience without muddying the raw fuzz tone.
blocks.gap: The requirement is for 'raw live Monterey bite,' so reverb must be kept minimal to avoid excessive bloom.

blocks.purpose: Final output level adjustment to ensure the raw signal is audible and punchy.

improvements.summary: Enhance cabinet realism to capture the raw, biting upper-mids of a live Monterey performance.

proposals.reason: Improve the raw, biting upper-mids and vintage character of the live sound.
